newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold kicks heels on sluggish Indian demand.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold kicks heels on sluggish Indian demand.

text.p: Rising bullion prices have taken the shine off Dubai's retail market which had seen turnover pick up in July on gold's slump to 12-year price lows, traders based in the Gulf Arab emirate said on Sunday.

Re-exports to India were also dulled by the monsoon season though levels remained supported by some Indian importers advancing their orders from August because of the recent downturn in prices, traders and wholesalers said.
"July has seen some good buying in the local market and into India but this has slowed down because of the turnaround in gold prices," said an Indian expatriate trader based in Dubai.
Dubai is the main feed supplier into India which is the world's single largest consumer of the yellow metal.
Indian import demand has followed its seasonal demand pattern this summer, falling since late June when rural farmers sow their cash crops with the onset on the monsoon rains.
Demand traditionally takes off with the festival and wedding seasons from September.
Dubai's benchmark TT bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- tracked spot prices higher and was quoted at 4,547 UAE dirhams ($1,238) on Sunday, up from 4,446 dirhams on July 13.
Spot gold was last quoted on Saturday at $328.60-329.10 an ounce, up from $321.20-70 a week earlier bouncing back from 12-year-lows on a recovery in physical buying.
Traders in Dubai said that there was room for further upside but cautioned that a move above $330 could prompt renewed bullion sales by central banks and funds.
"I'm still holding to my view that we are heading to resistance at $282," said one local trader.
Dubai-based dealers saw little immediate impact from news that the Pakistan government would open up the import of gold and silver in a bid to narrow its trade gap.
"It will be hard to attract new companies to supply the market...That market is so small compared to India and most of it is already supplied by smuggling," said one trader.
Currently only three firms have the permit into import gold into Pakistan.
Dubai's gold import figures for June are expected this week and are expected to show a seasonal slow-down in Indian and Gulf summer demand, traders said.
Traders expect imports to be 45-52 tonnes last month, compared to 52.29 tonnes in May.
"There is usually a downturn from June to August because India trims back because of the monsoons," said one trader.
Imports last summer fell back to an average of between 28-29 tonnes versus spring levels of 32-33 tonnes.
